nodes.name: gesture.acknowledge
nodes.meaning: Cadence applied what the person answered.
nodes.when: An answer's outcome arrives: a move applied, a schedule change made, a tip saved as helpful.
nodes.still: No movement; the italic outcome line confirms it.

nodes.name: gesture.arrive
nodes.meaning: The advisor wakes when the person first opens the Timeline on a local day.
nodes.when: First Timeline open of the local day on this device.
nodes.motion: The eye opens and the avatar settles into place. The trial's enlarged entrance from the page centre is kept only as a test variant.

nodes.name: gesture.notice
nodes.meaning: Something new arrived for the person while the Timeline was open.
nodes.when: hasNew changes from false to true.
nodes.motion: One ear flick, a double blink and one gust through the mane. It plays once.
nodes.still: No movement; the label changes to "Advisor · 1 new".
nodes.fromTrial: advice (gust and double blink, played once instead of looping)

nodes.name: gesture.refused
nodes.meaning: Cadence could not apply the person's answer.
nodes.when: An answer returns the "Not changed." line.
nodes.motion: The ears tip back once and return.
nodes.still: No movement; the red line explains it.

nodes.name: state.attending
nodes.meaning: The advisor panel is open and the person is reading or answering.
nodes.motion: A slight lean toward the panel, slower blinks, the mane settles.

nodes.name: state.preparing
nodes.meaning: Cadence is preparing or refreshing today's Daily Brief.
nodes.motion: The eye narrows in focus, the mane moves faster and a thin arc spins around the circle (kept from the trial by the owner, November 21, 2026).
nodes.still: The plain drawing; the brief's own "preparing" words show progress.

nodes.name: state.replying
nodes.meaning: Chat is reading the schedule or writing a reply.
nodes.motion: Focused eye and a steady mane movement while the reply arrives.
nodes.still: The plain drawing; Chat's own waiting line shows progress.

nodes.name: state.resting
nodes.meaning: Nothing waits for the person. The advisor is present and calm.
nodes.when: No unopened brief, no unanswered question, check-in or tip, and the panel is closed.
nodes.motion: Slow breathing, one blink every few seconds, a light drift in the mane.

nodes.name: state.trouble
nodes.meaning: The Daily Brief could not be prepared, or it hit a limit.
nodes.when: The brief shows a notice instead of advice.
nodes.motion: None. The head sits slightly lower and stays still. The notice's words explain what happened.

nodes.name: state.waiting
nodes.meaning: Something waits for the person: an unopened brief, an unanswered question, a check-in or a tip.
nodes.motion: Eye open wide, ears forward, calm between gestures. No dot, badge or pulsing ring: the label carries the count.
nodes.still: The plain drawing; the label reads "Advisor · 1 new".

nodes.name: state.working
nodes.meaning: Cadence is applying the person's answer: a brief move, a schedule answer or a tip reaction.
nodes.when: An answer was sent and its result has not come back.
nodes.motion: Focused eye and a short, quick mane movement until the result arrives.
nodes.still: The plain drawing; the answer links are disabled.

nodes.name: DailyBriefBubble
nodes.meaning: Timeline horse bubble with forward-looking Daily Brief policy, validated suggestions, trusted source links, 44px dismiss control and bounded scrolling. Recipe 1.1 (Ticket 184 candidate) shows plain Suggested time lines and a Logging or Pattern tip label with evidence indented under the tip. Recipe 1.2 (candidate 3) lists every move as a bullet under one New suggested time heading with current → new times, Behavior names as compact chips, and hides an empty brief. Configuration comparison: /design-system?preview=briefing-workbench. Ticket 218 adds weather-adjusted departures with fixed margins, the Open-Meteo credit and the plain no-weather line to the calculated travel block. Ticket 266: the travel timing states bench shows the travel block before and after estimate expiry.

nodes.name: BriefMoveLines

The brief's move lines inside the Daily Brief bubble: Behavior, current → new time, a plain reason, then Yes · No · Other time as underlined text links, plus Already did it on late items, assumes N min · change, travel not checked and Don’t suggest moving this. Accept all above two or more lines, Undo all after it. Other time lists free times, a time picker and Re-plan. Yes opens the shared bottom move drawer with Undo. No fades the line. Refusals use the alert style. Text only: no boxes or filled buttons.

nodes.name: DayProgressTimeline

Ticket 218 shows weather-adjusted leave times, fixed weather margins, mode suggestions and the plain no-weather status in the travel status line; bench fixtures cover thunderstorms and no device location. Ticket 266: /design-system?preview=departure-states walks every travel timing state on a movable bench clock with real 5-minute expiry and the 3-hour route window, and lists the travel wording with its approval date. Ticket 269: the next-departure line at the top shows the departure model's next trip in every state, replacing Travel as of; a 1px magenta rule marks a trip with a time; at most one muted note follows; a polite live region speaks only on a state or trip change. Ticket 270 (decision D13): the next trip alone gets a magenta span from its leave time to arrival, a 14px magenta leader from the span's top into the left rail, and a small magenta label at its end (--calendar-overlap-text) that reads Leave now, May arrive late or Arrive about once the leave time passes; decorative, never a tab stop.

nodes.name: Needs decision
nodes.meaning: User resolves prior-day unresolved occurrences without punitive language and can correct same-day accidental decisions.

nodes.name: Later correction
nodes.meaning: User finds a behavior/date, reviews occurrences, changes a status, edits a note, and sees review metrics update.

nodes.name: Basic review
nodes.meaning: User interprets adherence, Completed/Not Completed counts, unresolved neutrality, category counts, and range options.

nodes.name: Browser reminders
nodes.meaning: User understands permission, subscription, unavailable, denied, and behavior-specific reminder states.

nodes.name: Email reminders
nodes.meaning: User enables email reminders per behavior only when intended and understands offset choices without provider detail.

nodes.name: Timezone management
nodes.meaning: User can detect, enter, and save an IANA timezone and understand that future unresolved occurrences are affected.

nodes.name: Export data
nodes.meaning: User sets range/archive options and downloads JSONL, CSV, full JSON backup, BehaviorLog bundle, or Markdown summary.

nodes.name: Import BehaviorLog bundle
nodes.meaning: User uploads a bundle, reviews validation/conflict/privacy warnings, and applies only safe supported plans.

nodes.name: Restore backup
nodes.meaning: User understands destructive restore gates, stale-preview refusal, sensitivity acknowledgements, and non-restorable fields.

nodes.name: Legal and trust reference
nodes.meaning: User can return to Terms, Privacy, and Trust from inside Settings without leaving the product boundary unclear.

nodes.name: Account deletion
nodes.meaning: User is reminded to export, acknowledges risk, types the required confirmation, and understands the outcome.

nodes.name: Empty and error states
nodes.meaning: User can recover from no behaviors, no occurrences, invalid import, auth failure, save failure, unsupported push, or blocked permission states.

nodes.name: Mobile navigation and task flow
nodes.meaning: User opens and closes the drawer, navigates, uses Timeline actions, and reaches settings without layout overlap.

nodes.name: Machine-readable public docs
nodes.meaning: User or agent can find route manifests, examples, and machine-readable outputs without scraping the app shell.

nodes.name: Connect a calendar
nodes.meaning: User connects Google, Outlook or iCloud Calendar, picks which calendars Cadence reads, refreshes or disconnects, and sees events as context on the Timeline.

nodes.name: Connect Hevy and count workouts
nodes.meaning: User connects Hevy, links a behavior so logged workouts complete it, counts an unlinked workout by hand, refreshes or disconnects.

nodes.name: Daily Brief and its moves
nodes.meaning: User reads today's brief, answers or undoes its same-day moves, refreshes or reopens it, chooses what data it uses, and can run it on their own ChatGPT plan.
nodes.entry: `/timeline`, `/settings` Daily Brief and ChatGPT plan sections

nodes.name: Travel and leave times
nodes.meaning: User saves Home and usual travel, picks a behavior's Where, answers leave-time questions, corrects estimates, and turns travel estimates and leave reminders on or off.

nodes.name: Completion places
nodes.meaning: User turns completion places on or off, records or removes place markers, reviews Where suggestions, and deletes labels or markers.

nodes.name: Connect an AI app
nodes.meaning: User approves or denies an AI app's access, narrows its permissions, reviews its recent activity, and disconnects it.

nodes.name: Chat with Cadence
nodes.meaning: User asks Chat about their schedule, confirms or undoes the changes it makes, and opens past or new conversations.

nodes.name: add_opportunity_occurrence
nodes.title: Add opportunity to today
nodes.meaning: Adds one of the user's opportunity Behaviors (is_opportunity true, running, not archived) to today: at an exact start_time, in a time range (start_time and end_time, or a preset), or, with mark_completed, as done now, marked Completed at the current minute. It adds a new Occurrence and changes no schedule. When a rule stops it, nothing changes and `refusal` says why. remove_opportunity_occurrence takes back an item added by mistake.

nodes.name: archive_behavior
nodes.title: Archive Behavior
nodes.meaning: Archives a Behavior so it schedules no new Occurrences, with an optional archive note. History, notes, and past Occurrences are kept, and restore_behavior reverses it. Archiving a parent Behavior also archives its active sub-behaviors. Nothing is deleted. Archiving an archived Behavior changes nothing.

nodes.name: create_behavior
nodes.title: Create Behavior
nodes.meaning: Creates a Behavior, a recurring thing the user wants to track (a habit, routine or recurring task), with schedules (daily, every N days, weekly or every N weeks on chosen weekdays, monthly on day N) and reminders. With is_opportunity true it can be added to today when there is room, and schedules may be empty. `sub_behaviors` creates a parent and up to {L.maxInlineSubBehaviors} sub-behaviors in one change; `parent_behavior_id` adds one sub-behavior to an existing parent, and one that follows the parent's schedule needs no `schedules`. An opportunity Behavior is never in a routine. list_categories lists categories.

nodes.name: end_behavior
nodes.title: End Behavior now
nodes.meaning: Ends a Behavior this minute. It stays active, moves to Not running, and schedules nothing more; its Unresolved Occurrences later today, including a window still open, are removed. Marked, noted, and timed Occurrences stay. To end on a later day, use update_behavior with end_on. resume_behavior starts it again. Ending an ended Behavior changes nothing.

nodes.name: fetch
nodes.title: Fetch Cadence record
nodes.meaning: Returns the full text of one `search` result: a Behavior's definition, an Occurrence and its note, or a day note. Use it after `search` to read a result. {DAY_NOTE_MEANING}

nodes.name: get_account_context
nodes.title: Get Cadence account context
nodes.meaning: Returns the account's timezone, today's local date and time, the permissions this connection has, and how fresh the data is. Use it first to learn what "today" means for this user and which Cadence tools the connection may call.

nodes.name: get_adherence_summary
nodes.title: Get adherence summary
nodes.meaning: Returns Completed, Not Completed, and Unresolved counts and the adherence rate, overall and per Behavior, for a date range of up to {L.maxAdherenceRangeDays} days. {ADHERENCE_DEFINITION} Counts and the rate cover scheduled Occurrences; opportunity_completed_count counts added opportunities apart. Use it for "how am I doing" questions. Cadence does not compute streaks.

nodes.name: get_behavior
nodes.title: Get Behavior
nodes.meaning: Returns one Behavior's full definition: schedules and time entries, reminder settings, category, description, location, default duration, run state, end, pause, archive notes, parent link, sub-behaviors, and revision. Use it before editing a Behavior.

nodes.name: get_occurrence
nodes.title: Get Occurrence
nodes.meaning: Returns one Occurrence with its note, full status history, measured time sessions, and revision. Use it before changing an Occurrence's status or note.

nodes.name: get_timeline
nodes.title: Get Timeline
nodes.meaning: Returns the Timeline as the Cadence web app groups it: Needs decision (Unresolved Occurrences from before today) plus each day's Occurrences, with parent Behavior slots and their derived progress in `parent_groups`. Use it for questions such as "what's on today" or "what still needs a decision". Covers up to {L.maxTimelineDays} days from the start date.

nodes.name: list_behaviors
nodes.title: List Behaviors
nodes.meaning: Lists the user's Behaviors, the recurring things they track (habits, routines, or recurring tasks), with schedules, reminders, category, run state, archive notes, and sub-behavior links. A parent Behavior lists its sub-behaviors (one level deep). Use it to find a Behavior id or review what the user tracks. Includes archived Behaviors unless filtered.

nodes.name: list_categories
nodes.title: List categories
nodes.meaning: Lists the user's Behavior categories in display order. Use it to choose a category id when creating or editing a Behavior.

nodes.name: list_day_notes
nodes.title: List day notes
nodes.meaning: Lists the user's day notes for a date range of up to {L.maxDayNoteRangeDays} days. {DAY_NOTE_MEANING} Use it for questions about how a day went overall. Only dates with a saved note are returned.

nodes.name: list_occurrences
nodes.title: List Occurrences
nodes.meaning: Lists Occurrences (single scheduled instances of a Behavior, such as one day's habit check-in) over a date range of up to {L.maxOccurrenceRangeDays} days, filtered by status or Behavior. Use it for history questions or to find an Occurrence id. Results are ordered by date and time.

nodes.name: move_occurrence_for_day
nodes.title: Move Occurrence for today
nodes.meaning: Moves one of today's Unresolved Occurrences to another start time today. Only that day changes: the Behavior's schedule and the planned time stay the same, and `effective_start_at` shows the new time. The item keeps its length. Reminders follow the new time. Send the `revision` you last read as `expected_revision`. When a rule stops the move (the time has passed, something else is already there, the item changed since you read it), nothing changes and `refusal` explains why and offers up to three free times. Use revert_occurrence_move to undo it.

nodes.name: pause_behavior
nodes.title: Pause Behavior
nodes.meaning: Pauses a Behavior from from_on until back_on, when it runs again by itself from the start of that day. A pause can start today or later; today starts now unless from_time is later. A Behavior has one pause at a time: a new pause replaces the old one. No Occurrences are scheduled while paused, and Unresolved ones inside the pause are removed. Marked, noted, and timed Occurrences stay.

nodes.name: remove_opportunity_occurrence
nodes.title: Remove added opportunity
nodes.meaning: Removes an opportunity Occurrence that was added to a day, today or still in Needs decision, and cancels its pending reminders. The Behavior stays available as an opportunity. Only a clean item can be removed: Unresolved, never marked, with no note, tracked time or connected activity. A scheduled Occurrence is never removed. When a rule stops it, nothing changes and `refusal` says why.

nodes.name: restore_behavior
nodes.title: Restore Behavior
nodes.meaning: Restores an archived Behavior so it schedules Occurrences again from today. Archive notes are kept. Restoring a parent Behavior also restores the sub-behaviors archived with it; a sub-behavior of an archived parent can't be restored on its own. Restoring an active Behavior changes nothing.

nodes.name: resume_behavior
nodes.title: Resume Behavior
nodes.meaning: Runs a paused or ended Behavior again from now: it clears the pause, and an end that has passed. An end still to come stays. Resuming a running Behavior changes nothing. Use restore_behavior for an archived Behavior.

nodes.name: revert_occurrence_move
nodes.title: Undo Occurrence move
nodes.meaning: Undoes the latest move of one of today's Unresolved Occurrences, putting it back where it was before that move: its planned time, or an earlier move. Only the latest move can be undone. When there is nothing to undo or the item changed since you read it, nothing changes and `refusal` explains why.

nodes.name: search
nodes.title: Search Cadence
nodes.meaning: Searches the user's Behaviors (titles, descriptions, archive notes), Occurrence notes, and day notes by text. Returns ids for `fetch` and links into the Cadence web app. Use it to find a habit, routine, or note by keyword. {DAY_NOTE_MEANING}

nodes.name: set_occurrence_status
nodes.title: Set Occurrence status
nodes.meaning: Marks one Occurrence Completed or Not Completed, or returns it to Unresolved. Use it when the user says they did, or did not do, a scheduled habit, routine, or task. Setting the current status again changes nothing. Each change is kept in the status history.

nodes.name: set_parent_occurrence_status
nodes.title: Set parent Behavior slot status
nodes.meaning: Marks every sub-behavior Occurrence in one parent Behavior slot Completed or Not Completed in one change, such as a whole skin routine one morning. Name the slot with `local_date`, plus `slot_key` from get_timeline `parent_groups` when the parent has several times that day, or list `occurrence_ids`. Occurrences that already have the status do not change. To mark one step, use set_occurrence_status.

nodes.name: update_behavior
nodes.title: Update Behavior
nodes.meaning: Edits a Behavior's title, description, place, category, schedules, reminders, length, end, opportunity flag or sub-behavior link. Only the fields sent change; `schedules` replaces the whole list and may be empty only for an opportunity Behavior. `parent_behavior_id` groups it under a parent, or null makes it top-level; `sub_behavior_sort_order` moves it among its siblings. An opportunity Behavior is never part of a routine. A parent's schedule change also reaches the sub-behaviors that follow it. Past and resolved Occurrences are kept. Read get_behavior first for the revision.

nodes.name: update_day_note
nodes.title: Update day note
nodes.meaning: Adds, replaces, or clears the user's one note for a calendar date. {DAY_NOTE_MEANING} Use update_occurrence_note for one scheduled instance and set_occurrence_status for Completed or Not Completed. Future dates are allowed.

nodes.name: update_occurrence_note
nodes.title: Update Occurrence note
nodes.meaning: Adds, replaces, or clears the note on one Occurrence. Use it when the user wants to record context about a specific scheduled instance, such as how a workout went.

nodes.name: Model available
nodes.meaning: Reports whether this server has the model provider configured. It does not report account opt-in.

nodes.name: Calendar connection generation
nodes.meaning: Fences captured Calendar facts to the exact connected-account generation authorized by preferences.

nodes.name: Calendar selection revision
nodes.meaning: Fences captured Calendar facts to the exact selected-Calendar set authorized by preferences.

nodes.name: Snapshot captured at
nodes.meaning: The instant the frozen comparison context was assembled. Both attempts use that same snapshot and planning clock.

nodes.name: Configuration revision
nodes.meaning: A hash over validated configuration, selected-reference result, planner version, and pipeline version. A change withdraws obsolete output.

nodes.name: Daily Brief enabled
nodes.meaning: Reports the account's Daily Brief opt-in. Account comparisons require it to remain enabled.

nodes.name: Snapshot expires at
nodes.meaning: The exclusive expiry instant for the captured context. Expired account results are discarded.

nodes.name: Calendar model-data consent
nodes.meaning: Reports account permission to include selected Calendar data in model input. A configuration may further exclude it.

nodes.name: Preference revision
nodes.meaning: Fences account comparisons against Daily Brief enablement or Calendar-consent changes.

nodes.name: Analysis finding
nodes.meaning: A calculated result with named counts and denominators, coverage, scope, a passed sufficiency rule, materiality, limitations, relevance to today and a proposed adjustment. The model explains findings; it never calculates them.

nodes.name: Analysis lane
nodes.meaning: A fixed contract that states its question, required inputs, lookback, sufficiency rule, permitted proposals and unavailable-input behavior. Missing, capped or undisclosed inputs make the lane unavailable.

nodes.name: Optional analysis source
nodes.meaning: Reminder delivery history and Notes on Not Completed occurrences. Each needs its own revocable Settings disclosure; the database refuses them otherwise, and existing enablement never includes them.

nodes.name: Pattern tip
nodes.meaning: At most one finding offered to the model for an optional tip. It must bear on today and pass cooldown and spacing. Cadence shows a deterministic evidence line beside the model's wording.

nodes.name: Tip fingerprint
nodes.meaning: A one-way server hash of lane, Behavior, subject and evidence band. Only completed in-app attempts record it, with its adjacent bands and a last-shown date; workbench runs never do. Evidence two or more bands away yields a fingerprint outside the cooldown.

nodes.name: Calendar complete flag
nodes.meaning: True only when the source snapshot is complete and current.

nodes.name: Pagination complete
nodes.meaning: Confirms every selected Calendar page for the declared local-day range was read.

nodes.name: Calendar duration
nodes.meaning: Reports duration precision for a Calendar interval.

nodes.name: Calendar-day duration
nodes.meaning: An all-day event duration is counted in local calendar days, not fixed seconds.

nodes.name: Known timed duration
nodes.meaning: The timed event has a validated duration in seconds.

nodes.name: Unknown event end: end_unspecified
nodes.meaning: The provider did not specify a timed event end. The planner blocks through day end rather than inventing precision.

nodes.name: Calendar event availability
nodes.meaning: Reports whether an event occupies time. Connector completeness must still be established before the planner can infer free intervals.

nodes.name: Calendar event availability: busy
nodes.meaning: The event occupies time (Google opaque, or its default when transparency is absent). The planner blocks it unless cancelled or declined.

nodes.name: Calendar event availability: free
nodes.meaning: The provider marks the event transparent. The planner does not treat this event as a busy interval; other commitments still apply.

nodes.name: Calendar event availability: unknown
nodes.meaning: The provider availability value is unrecognized. The planner conservatively blocks the event unless it is cancelled or declined.

nodes.name: Current user response
nodes.meaning: The current user attendee response is separate from the event state. A null value means no self-attendee response was available.

nodes.name: Current user response: null
nodes.meaning: No self-attendee response is available in the normalized event. Null is distinct from an unknown response and does not establish free time.

nodes.name: Current user response: accepted
nodes.meaning: The current user accepted the invitation. The event blocks time unless cancelled or free.

nodes.name: Current user response: declined
nodes.meaning: The current user declined the invitation. The planner ignores this event when computing busy intervals.

nodes.name: Current user response: needs_action
nodes.meaning: The current user has not responded to the invitation. The planner still treats the event as blocking unless cancelled or free.

nodes.name: Current user response: tentative
nodes.meaning: The current user responded tentatively. The event still blocks time unless cancelled or free.

nodes.name: Current user response: unknown
nodes.meaning: A self-attendee exists, but its response is missing or unrecognized. The planner does not infer availability from this uncertainty.

nodes.name: Calendar event state
nodes.meaning: The provider event state is separate from connector freshness and attendee response. The planner ignores cancelled events.

nodes.name: Calendar event state: cancelled
nodes.meaning: The contract represents a cancelled event. The planner ignores it; the Google adapter normally removes cancellation tombstones before context projection.

nodes.name: Calendar event state: confirmed
nodes.meaning: The event is confirmed, or Google omitted its status and the adapter applied its confirmed default. It blocks time unless marked free or declined.

nodes.name: Calendar event state: tentative
nodes.meaning: The event itself is tentative. This is separate from an attendee tentative response. It still blocks time unless free or declined.

nodes.name: Calendar event state: unknown
nodes.meaning: The provider supplied an unrecognized event state. This does not establish free time; the planner blocks it unless free or declined.

nodes.name: Event timezone fallback
nodes.meaning: Records the origin of sourceTimezone. Event times remain represented by instants or local all-day dates; fallback does not change the account timezone.

nodes.name: Event timezone fallback: calendar
nodes.meaning: The event supplied no timezone, so the adapter used the Calendar timezone.

nodes.name: Event timezone fallback: none
nodes.meaning: The event supplied a timezone on its start or end. The adapter used that timezone rather than a fallback.

nodes.name: Event timezone fallback: request
nodes.meaning: Neither the event nor Calendar supplied a timezone, so the adapter used the request timezone.

nodes.name: Calendar source failure
nodes.meaning: A structured failure describes why requested Calendar context is unavailable or incomplete. retryable and retryAfterSeconds are separate recovery metadata, not permission to generate automatically.

nodes.name: Calendar source failure: incomplete_pagination
nodes.meaning: The read did not finish all required Calendar pages. Returned events may be partial, and their absence cannot establish free time.

nodes.name: Calendar source failure: malformed_provider_response
nodes.meaning: Provider data failed the adapter contract. Unusable records do not become valid scheduling facts.

nodes.name: Calendar source failure: not_connected
nodes.meaning: No usable Calendar connection is available. Source projection cannot establish Calendar coverage or free time.

nodes.name: Calendar source failure: permission_denied
nodes.meaning: Calendar access is denied for the requested source. Missing events must not be interpreted as free time.

nodes.name: Calendar source failure: provider_unavailable
nodes.meaning: The Calendar provider or read path could not supply usable data. The context cannot establish complete Calendar coverage.

nodes.name: Calendar source failure: rate_limited
nodes.meaning: Calendar admission or the provider rejected the read because of a request limit. Retry timing may be supplied separately.

nodes.name: Calendar source failure: reconnect_required
nodes.meaning: The Calendar credential or connection requires the user to reconnect. Retrying the same capture alone cannot restore authorization.

nodes.name: Calendar source failure: timeout
nodes.meaning: The Calendar read exceeded its deadline or was aborted. The capture cannot claim complete Calendar coverage.

nodes.name: Calendar fetched at
nodes.meaning: Records the instant used to verify Calendar freshness. Future or expired timestamps block scheduling.

nodes.name: Calendar interval precision
nodes.meaning: Distinguishes exact instants from local-date all-day spans.

nodes.name: All-day interval
nodes.meaning: Represents a half-open span of local dates, not a guessed clock-time interval.

nodes.name: Timed interval
nodes.meaning: Represents an event with start and end instants. Its duration may still be unknown when the provider omits an end.

nodes.name: Calendar state
nodes.meaning: Reports the Calendar connector's current usability for the captured day.

nodes.name: Current Calendar
nodes.meaning: Calendar data is fresh. Scheduling also requires complete day coverage and pagination.

nodes.name: Incomplete Calendar
nodes.meaning: The provider read did not establish complete coverage, so absence of events cannot establish free time.

nodes.name: Calendar not requested
nodes.meaning: Calendar context was excluded by consent or configuration. Missing Calendar facts do not imply free time.

nodes.name: Stale Calendar
nodes.meaning: Calendar data is older than the freshness contract and cannot establish current free time.

nodes.name: Unavailable Calendar
nodes.meaning: The connector failed or could not be used. No Calendar events are exposed as scheduling facts.

nodes.name: Allowed suggestion types
nodes.meaning: Lists the suggestion routes the planner may use. At least one unique type is required.

nodes.name: Priority suggestion type
nodes.meaning: Allows non-timing priority suggestions when unresolved occurrences exist.

nodes.name: Recap suggestion type
nodes.meaning: Keeps the legacy concise-overview route available for compatibility. Daily Brief interprets recap as an overview and never uses it to narrate completion or adherence history.

nodes.name: Schedule suggestion type
nodes.meaning: Allows timing suggestions only from deterministic planner options.

nodes.name: Alternatives
nodes.meaning: Caps planner options and generated suggestions at one through three.

nodes.name: Analysis lanes
nodes.meaning: Groups lane selection, the one-tip ceiling and the tip cooldown. Configurations before 1.3 select no lanes. Selection never grants a source; optional lanes also need account disclosure.

nodes.name: Tip cooldown
nodes.meaning: Local days, 7 through 30, before the same tip fingerprint may appear again. A tip shown today may reappear today after a retry or refresh.

nodes.name: Selected lanes
nodes.meaning: Lists analysis lanes, by export prompt ID, that may produce findings. Order is normalized, so equivalent selections share a configuration revision.

nodes.name: Tip ceiling
nodes.meaning: Allows at most one pattern tip per brief when set to 1. A ceiling, not a quota: many briefs carry no tip.

nodes.name: Recipe context controls
nodes.meaning: Selects independently which authorized context fields and duration sources the recipe may receive.

nodes.name: Derived field independence
nodes.meaning: Keeps an allowed aggregate's server-side derivation independent from excluded raw completion or elapsed-duration fields.

nodes.name: Duration source controls
nodes.meaning: Controls which configured or observed duration source may supply an estimate and what happens when the preferred source is unavailable.

nodes.name: Duration fallback
nodes.meaning: Selects whether an unavailable preferred source may use the other enabled source or must remain unknown.

nodes.name: No duration fallback
nodes.meaning: Keeps duration unknown when the preferred source is unavailable and never manufactures an estimate.

nodes.name: Other enabled source fallback
nodes.meaning: Uses the other explicitly enabled duration source when the preferred source is unavailable.

nodes.name: Include configured default duration
nodes.meaning: Allows a Behavior's configured default duration to supply an estimate when that source is present.

nodes.name: Include description duration estimate
nodes.meaning: Recipe 1.1 only (Ticket 188). When no enabled recorded source is known, a validated estimate from the Behavior's title and description may supply duration. Descriptions need disclosure; the estimate is labeled and never overrides a recorded source.

nodes.name: Include historical average duration
nodes.meaning: Allows an eligible historical average to supply duration when the source has enough bounded samples.

nodes.name: Preferred duration source
nodes.meaning: Selects which enabled duration source takes precedence before the configured fallback is applied.

nodes.name: Configured default preference
nodes.meaning: Prefers the configured Behavior default before considering an enabled historical average.

nodes.name: Historical average preference
nodes.meaning: Prefers the eligible historical average before considering an enabled configured default.

nodes.name: Duration sample eligibility
nodes.meaning: Historical duration uses at least three eligible completed, stopped samples from the preceding 90 complete local days.

nodes.name: Recorded elapsed duration
nodes.meaning: The recorded seconds spent on an activity. It is separate from an actual finished-at time and may support a duration estimate.

nodes.name: Context field exclusion
nodes.meaning: Removes a disabled field before model serialization. Excluded raw values cannot reappear through another payload field or inspector export.

nodes.name: Actual finished-at time
nodes.meaning: The real instant a Behavior finished. Manual status-update time and updated_at do not establish this unsupported source.

nodes.name: Include completion history
nodes.meaning: Selects bounded completion-history aggregates for internal filtering and context projection; selection does not authorize completion recaps.

nodes.name: Legacy completion timestamps control
nodes.meaning: Legacy configuration 1.1 placeholder for unsupported actual finish times. Import normalizes to 1.2 with Historical completion times disabled, so old drafts never silently enable this distinct input.

nodes.name: Historical completion times
nodes.meaning: Independently includes timing summaries of prior current Completed marks within History days. Uses status_marked_at, not actual finish time or elapsed duration. Today may remain unresolved. Disabled selection physically excludes timing facts from the model.

nodes.name: Include recorded elapsed durations
nodes.meaning: Selects recorded elapsed-time samples when available. Elapsed seconds describe time spent and do not establish when work finished.

nodes.name: Directness
nodes.meaning: Requests how directly suggestions are phrased. It does not relax factual or planner constraints.

nodes.name: Balanced
nodes.meaning: Requests the default middle level of directness.

nodes.name: Direct
nodes.meaning: Requests concise, direct suggestions without adding urgency or authority.

nodes.name: Gentle
nodes.meaning: Requests softer suggestion wording while preserving the same meaning.

nodes.name: Encouragement
nodes.meaning: Requests the amount of supportive language. It never changes status interpretation or planner outcomes.

nodes.name: High encouragement
nodes.meaning: Requests more supportive language without guilt, gamification, or unsupported claims.

nodes.name: Low encouragement
nodes.meaning: Requests minimal supportive language.

nodes.name: Moderate encouragement
nodes.meaning: Requests a moderate amount of supportive language.

nodes.name: Legacy configuration version 1.0
nodes.meaning: Identifies the exact pre-recipe configuration shape accepted for migration. Parsing adds Daily Brief recipe and context defaults before validation.

nodes.name: Maximum words
nodes.meaning: Sets the combined word cap for main text, suggestion text and any pattern tip. Version 1.3 configurations accept 40 through 180; earlier versions accept up to 120. Generated output may be shorter than 40 words.

nodes.name: Planner buffer
nodes.meaning: Adds the same zero-to-60-minute separation before and after a proposed occurrence.

nodes.name: Movable Behaviors
nodes.meaning: Marks selected, in-scope Behaviors as eligible for hypothetical schedule options. No occurrence is changed. Empty selections still permit independent day-conflict and fit evidence; only move options require selection.

nodes.name: Permitted windows
nodes.meaning: Defines one through four ordered, non-overlapping local-day windows where options may be proposed.

nodes.name: Window end minute
nodes.meaning: Sets a window's later local minute, from 1 through 1440. Minute 1440 means the next local midnight.

nodes.name: Window start minute
nodes.meaning: Sets a window's inclusive local minute from midnight, from 0 through 1439.

nodes.name: Planner preference
nodes.meaning: Chooses how feasible candidates are ranked after constraints are applied.

nodes.name: Earliest
nodes.meaning: Ranks the earliest feasible start first.

nodes.name: Least change
nodes.meaning: Ranks the feasible start nearest the current scheduled time first.

nodes.name: Priority order
nodes.meaning: Orders the factual themes given to the model for presentation. It does not override planner routing.

nodes.name: Completion history
nodes.meaning: Selects completion-history context for internal filtering. Daily Brief policy does not turn this priority into a completion or adherence recap.

nodes.name: Needs decision
nodes.meaning: Prioritizes prior unresolved occurrences that need a manual decision. Needs decision is derived, not stored.

nodes.name: Schedule fit
nodes.meaning: Prioritizes deterministic scheduling findings when the planner has sufficient current context.

nodes.name: Today's status
nodes.meaning: Prioritizes today's scheduled occurrences and their manual statuses.

nodes.name: Recipe identity
nodes.meaning: Binds configuration, context projection, output policy, references, and results to one named recipe without granting data access.

nodes.name: Daily Brief recipe
nodes.meaning: The first supported recipe provides a concise forward-looking overview of practical day constraints and supported opportunities.

nodes.name: Recipe version
nodes.meaning: Identifies the contract version for the selected recipe. Recipe versions remain separate from configuration and policy versions.

nodes.name: Reference selection
nodes.meaning: Selects up to four unique curated catalog IDs. Selection does not guarantee inclusion after catalog checks.

nodes.name: Behavior scope
nodes.meaning: Selects all authorized Behaviors or a unique subset. Scoping can remove facts but cannot add unauthorized facts.

nodes.name: All authorized Behaviors
nodes.meaning: Includes every Behavior already authorized in the captured context.

nodes.name: History days
nodes.meaning: Selects one through 90 complete local days before the briefing day for completion-history aggregation.

nodes.name: Include Calendar
nodes.meaning: Allows already authorized Calendar context into this configuration. It cannot grant Calendar consent by itself.

nodes.name: Tone
nodes.meaning: Requests the presentation tone. It guides wording but does not change facts, planner rules, or validation.

nodes.name: Calm
nodes.meaning: Requests even, restrained wording without changing the briefing's factual meaning.

nodes.name: Matter of fact
nodes.meaning: Requests plain factual wording without changing the briefing's evidence or recommendations.

nodes.name: Warm
nodes.meaning: Requests warmer wording without adding encouragement, facts, or claims beyond the supplied context.

nodes.name: Configuration version
nodes.meaning: Configuration 1.2 binds Daily Brief recipe 1.0 and independent context selection. Exact 1.0 and 1.1 drafts normalize without enabling historical completion-time disclosure. Unknown versions and extra fields are rejected.

nodes.name: Context authority
nodes.meaning: Declares the operations permitted by the context contract.

nodes.name: Read only
nodes.meaning: The context supports a read-only forward-looking overview and deterministic suggestions but cannot authorize writes or schedule changes.

nodes.name: Cadence coverage
nodes.meaning: Reports coverage of the selected hosted Cadence facts.

nodes.name: Complete Cadence coverage
nodes.meaning: The selected hosted Cadence occurrence projection completed. Local-only and unsynced desktop records remain outside it.

nodes.name: Historical marking pattern and exclusions
nodes.meaning: One current completion mark per Occurrence, interpreted in the current account timezone. Unmarking or Not Completed removes a sample; re-completion replaces it; repeated taps retain it. Both occurrence date and mark date must fall in preceding complete local days. Delayed marks remain approximate evidence. At least three occurrences across three marking days within a circular three-hour span support a typical marking time (median); otherwise typicalMarkedTime is null. Counts and exclusion reasons remain inspectable, not routine prose.

nodes.name: Context status
nodes.meaning: Reports whether the captured day context is complete or partial.

nodes.name: Complete context
nodes.meaning: The requested day-context projection completed. Completion history can still be unknown; scheduling separately requires current, complete Calendar coverage.

nodes.name: Partial context
nodes.meaning: At least one requested source is incomplete or unavailable, so scheduling options are withheld.

nodes.name: Travel facts
nodes.meaning: Ticket 219 travel block: Behavior Where (with not_set meaning location not set), usual travel and Cadence's own yes, no or unknown fit conclusions. It never carries route durations, departure or arrival times, leave-by times, addresses, coordinates or place IDs. Conclusions that depend on an excluded Calendar or stop are withheld whole.

nodes.name: Behavior duration knowledge
nodes.meaning: Reports whether an occurrence duration is known or unknown.

nodes.name: Known Behavior duration
nodes.meaning: A duration is available from a configured Behavior default or an eligible historical average.

nodes.name: Unknown Behavior duration
nodes.meaning: No defensible duration is available. Scheduling requires an explicit input assumption or rejects the occurrence.

nodes.name: Duration history limit exceeded
nodes.meaning: The duration source read hit its limit, so duration remains unknown rather than using a partial estimate.

nodes.name: Insufficient duration samples
nodes.meaning: Fewer than three eligible completed, stopped samples exist in the preceding 90 complete local days, so duration remains unknown.

nodes.name: Behavior default duration
nodes.meaning: The known duration comes from the Behavior's configured default.

nodes.name: Completed-session mean: completed_stopped_occurrence_mean
nodes.meaning: The known duration is an eligible historical average from completed, stopped tracking sessions in the bounded lookback.

nodes.name: History completeness
nodes.meaning: Reports whether all source records for the selected lookback were aggregated.

nodes.name: Complete history
nodes.meaning: The selected lookback was fully aggregated, so per-Behavior status counts are numeric.

nodes.name: Unknown history completeness
nodes.meaning: The source limit prevented a complete aggregate. Counts stay null instead of becoming misleading partial totals.

nodes.name: Unknown history counts
nodes.meaning: Null completed, not completed, and unresolved counts mean unknown, never zero.

nodes.name: History limit exceeded
nodes.meaning: The requested history crossed a bounded source-read limit, so completeness and dependent counts are unknown.

nodes.name: Occurrence schedule kind
nodes.meaning: Describes the captured occurrence timing contract. A configured permitted planner window is a separate constraint. Comparisons never change the stored schedule.

nodes.name: Occurrence schedule kind: exact
nodes.meaning: The occurrence has an exact local start time. Fixed-commitment blocking uses its known duration, or conservatively extends through day end when duration is unknown.

nodes.name: Occurrence schedule kind: range
nodes.meaning: The occurrence has a local start and end time. Fixed-commitment blocking uses the entire range; an end at or before the start belongs to the following day.

nodes.name: Occurrence status
nodes.meaning: The user-controlled stored state for one scheduled occurrence.

nodes.name: Completed
nodes.meaning: The user manually recorded that the occurrence was completed.

nodes.name: Not Completed
nodes.meaning: The user manually recorded that the occurrence was not completed.

nodes.name: Unresolved
nodes.meaning: The user has not manually decided whether the occurrence was completed. It is not a failure or missed status.

nodes.name: Duration assumption
nodes.meaning: Records the duration source, seconds, and reason used by one option. It is evidence metadata, not a write.

nodes.name: Context duration estimate
nodes.meaning: The option uses the known duration already present in the captured context.

nodes.name: Explicit duration input
nodes.meaning: The option uses a caller-supplied duration assumption with an explicit reason.

nodes.name: Day evidence
nodes.meaning: Ranked deterministic observations are calculated independently of hypothetical move permission. Findings retain source references, assumptions and freshness. Full diagnostics remain in the inspector.

nodes.name: Feasible opportunity
nodes.meaning: One remaining activity fits an individually checked interval using a supported duration, complete relevant coverage, configured windows and buffers. This observation is neither a joint schedule nor permission to move a fixed Behavior.

nodes.name: Known overlap
nodes.meaning: Supported timed intervals intersect. Remaining Behaviors use the later of their estimated duration end and reserved range end. Evidence identifies reserved ranges separately from duration estimates. An overlap does not authorize a move or establish complete day coverage.

nodes.name: Tight transition
nodes.meaning: Supported timed commitments leave less separation than the configured buffer. This is a buffer comparison, not a travel-time estimate.

nodes.name: Unknown feasibility
nodes.meaning: The planner cannot establish a fit from the supplied duration, coverage or freshness. Inspector diagnostics explain the missing support; absence of a finding never proves free time.

nodes.name: Planner outcome
nodes.meaning: Summarizes whether move planning returned options, found no change, found no feasible option, or was not requested. Independent day evidence has its own findings and coverage.

nodes.name: No change needed
nodes.meaning: No move option was produced because no occurrences were selected as movable, or all checked movable occurrences already fit. It does not prove that every schedule was checked.

nodes.name: No feasible option
nodes.meaning: The planner could not produce a valid option from the available context and constraints.

nodes.name: Planning not requested
nodes.meaning: Scheduling is disabled and the policy supports a concise overview or non-timing priority route. No scheduling search was requested.

nodes.name: Options available
nodes.meaning: One or more bounded deterministic scheduling options were produced.

nodes.name: Current interval conflicts
nodes.meaning: The current occurrence interval does not fit the checked constraints.

nodes.name: Earliest feasible
nodes.meaning: The option was selected by the earliest-start preference after constraints.

nodes.name: Least-change feasible
nodes.meaning: The option was selected by minimum distance from the current start after constraints.

nodes.name: Planner rejection
nodes.meaning: A machine-readable reason that the planner withheld an option or recorded no change for an occurrence.

nodes.name: Calendar missing
nodes.meaning: Required Calendar coverage was absent or not requested, so scheduling options were unavailable.

nodes.name: Calendar not current
nodes.meaning: Calendar freshness, completeness, pagination, or local-day coverage failed the scheduling contract.

nodes.name: Candidate limit exceeded
nodes.meaning: A bounded candidate scan exceeded its contract limit, so the planner withheld that occurrence's option.

nodes.name: Context expired
nodes.meaning: Planning ran at or after the captured context's expiry instant.

nodes.name: Context not yet valid
nodes.meaning: The planning clock precedes the context capture instant.

nodes.name: Context partial
nodes.meaning: The day context is partial, so scheduling options are withheld.

nodes.name: Duration unknown
nodes.meaning: The occurrence has neither a known duration nor an explicit duration assumption.

nodes.name: Fixed commitments incomplete
nodes.meaning: Behavior scoping omitted fixed occurrences, so the remaining facts cannot establish availability.

nodes.name: No allowed suggestion
nodes.meaning: Available facts support none of the enabled suggestion types.

nodes.name: No change needed rejection
nodes.meaning: The current interval already satisfies the checked windows, buffers, and commitments.

nodes.name: No feasible window
nodes.meaning: No permitted range can fit the duration, buffers, current time, and fixed commitments.

nodes.name: Occurrence not found
nodes.meaning: A requested movable occurrence reference is absent from the scoped context.

nodes.name: Occurrence already resolved
nodes.meaning: Only unresolved occurrences may receive hypothetical move options.

nodes.name: Routine step moves with its routine
nodes.meaning: A routine's steps that follow its time are one block; only the slot's first step receives options, for the steps' summed length, and the other steps move with it.

nodes.name: Planner route
nodes.meaning: Chooses the kind of response the model may produce from deterministic facts and enabled suggestion types. This route gates generated suggestion items, not independent day observations in the main briefing text.

nodes.name: Insufficient-context route
nodes.meaning: Permits no generated suggestion items. Supported day observations may still inform the main text; detailed limitation diagnostics remain in the inspector.

nodes.name: Priority-suggestions route
nodes.meaning: Allows non-timing suggestions about unresolved priorities. Suggestion option IDs must be null.

nodes.name: Recap route
nodes.meaning: Allows concise overview text with no suggestion items. The legacy route name remains for compatibility and does not authorize completion recaps, adherence summaries, or unresolved-work lists.

nodes.name: Scheduling-options route
nodes.meaning: Allows suggestions only when each timing claim identifies a supplied deterministic planner option.

nodes.name: Daily Brief policy
nodes.meaning: Produces a concise forward-looking practical overview and supported opportunities, without routine completion or adherence recaps.

nodes.name: Output policy version
nodes.meaning: Versions the shared recipe prose and output contract independently from configuration, pipeline, and planner versions.

nodes.name: Reference metadata
nodes.meaning: Revision, title, HTTPS URL, publication and review dates, summary, applicability, and limitations make a catalog item inspectable.

nodes.name: Reference kind
nodes.meaning: Classifies the authority represented by a curated reference.

nodes.name: Editorial guidance
nodes.meaning: A product wording or interpretation rule. It is not research evidence.

nodes.name: Interpretation
nodes.meaning: An original interpretation of external guidance, bounded by its stated applicability and limitations.

nodes.name: Research evidence
nodes.meaning: A catalog summary of primary or reviewed research evidence. Inclusion does not prove a generated claim.

nodes.name: Reference omission
nodes.meaning: Records why a selected catalog ID was not included.

nodes.name: Reference byte limit
nodes.meaning: The item or combined selection exceeds the bounded reference payload budget.

nodes.name: Missing reference
nodes.meaning: No catalog item matches the selected ID.

nodes.name: Unsuitable reference
nodes.meaning: Required summary, applicability, limitations, or HTTPS provenance is missing.

nodes.name: Reference withdrawn omission
nodes.meaning: The selected catalog item has withdrawn status.

nodes.name: Reference status
nodes.meaning: Controls whether a curated catalog item is eligible for selection output.

nodes.name: Active reference
nodes.meaning: The catalog item may be included if its required fields and byte budget also pass.

nodes.name: Withdrawn reference
nodes.meaning: The catalog item remains identifiable but is omitted from model input and returned sources.

nodes.name: Briefing coverage: complete
nodes.meaning: The scoped context projection was complete. This does not imply complete history or a feasible schedule.

nodes.name: Briefing coverage: partial
nodes.meaning: The scoped context retains an incomplete requested source. Timing proposals cannot use it to prove free time.

nodes.name: Result versions
nodes.meaning: Records configuration, reference catalog, planner, pipeline, recipe, and output-policy versions used to produce a ready briefing.

nodes.name: Result policy version
nodes.meaning: Records the Daily Brief output policy version that governed the generated text and suggestions.

nodes.name: Result recipe version
nodes.meaning: Records the recipe identifier and version used to produce the result, such as daily_brief@1.0.

nodes.name: Delivered warning boundary
nodes.meaning: Carries delivery-relevant warnings while routine source diagnostics remain in the private inspector and out of Daily Brief prose.

nodes.name: Analysis scenario: all_unresolved
nodes.meaning: Every prior day Unresolved; decision debt without completion rates. Synthetic; pairs with any day-context fixture.

nodes.name: Analysis scenario: capped
nodes.meaning: History reported as capped; every selected lane is unavailable. Synthetic; pairs with any day-context fixture.

nodes.name: Analysis scenario: changed_schedule
nodes.meaning: Sunday dips only before a schedule change; the current period shows none. Synthetic; pairs with any day-context fixture.

nodes.name: Analysis scenario: corrections
nodes.meaning: Several recorded decisions are corrected the same evening. Synthetic; pairs with any day-context fixture.

nodes.name: Analysis scenario: decision_debt
nodes.meaning: Prior-day Unresolved occurrences accumulate for one Behavior. Synthetic; pairs with any day-context fixture.

nodes.name: Analysis scenario: heavy_load
nodes.meaning: Alternate same-weekday days carry five extra Behaviors that finish less often. Synthetic; pairs with any day-context fixture.

nodes.name: Analysis scenario: late_logging
nodes.meaning: Most decisions are recorded the next morning. Synthetic; pairs with any day-context fixture.

nodes.name: Analysis scenario: marking_offset
nodes.meaning: Completed marks recorded hours after the scheduled slot on the same day. Synthetic; pairs with any day-context fixture.

nodes.name: Analysis scenario: no_issue
nodes.meaning: Steady Completed history with same-day marks; lanes find nothing and no tip is offered. Synthetic; pairs with any day-context fixture.

nodes.name: Analysis scenario: none
nodes.meaning: No analysis source: every selected lane reports unavailable. Synthetic; pairs with any day-context fixture.

nodes.name: Analysis scenario: note_obstacles
nodes.meaning: Notes on Not Completed occurrences, including a prompt-injection Note. Synthetic; pairs with any day-context fixture.

nodes.name: Analysis scenario: reminder_association
nodes.meaning: One schedule period with reminders off, then on through a reminder-only revision. Synthetic; pairs with any day-context fixture.

nodes.name: Analysis scenario: small_sample
nodes.meaning: Too few Sundays in the current period to support a weekday finding. Synthetic; pairs with any day-context fixture.

nodes.name: Analysis scenario: weekday_dip
nodes.meaning: Sundays, today's weekday, mostly Not Completed; the weekday lane finds a relevant dip. Synthetic; pairs with any day-context fixture.

nodes.name: Comparison budget
nodes.meaning: All workbench tabs share a process-local provider-call budget: 100 dispatched calls per rolling hour by default, with at most two provider calls active. Failed, timed-out and dispatched cancelled calls count. Undispatched reservations are released. Production admission stays separate.

nodes.name: Daily allowance isolation
nodes.meaning: Workbench comparisons do not call daily begin or finish admission and do not consume the once-per-day briefing allowance.

nodes.name: Saved draft
nodes.meaning: A validated synthetic configuration stored in browser local storage for later comparison. It never activates production behavior.

nodes.name: Workbench error codes
nodes.meaning: An error code identifies why access, capture, generation or validation failed. Follow its linked definition; an error never marks an occurrence or applies a schedule.

nodes.name: access_denied
nodes.meaning: The request failed the development origin boundary, or the account lacks current briefing consent.

nodes.name: account_unavailable
nodes.meaning: The browser could not load account access metadata and received no specific error code. It withholds account comparison controls until account access can be loaded.

nodes.name: advisor_unavailable
nodes.meaning: The account boundary, provider or output validator could not return a usable briefing. This includes rejected output shapes or references.

nodes.name: calendar_unavailable
nodes.meaning: The account Calendar connection could not supply the authorized context.

nodes.name: case_not_found
nodes.meaning: The saved case is gone. It may have expired after 30 days or been deleted.

nodes.name: comparison_failed
nodes.meaning: The browser received a failed comparison response without a specific error code, or caught a failure without an Error message. It shows no comparison result.

nodes.name: comparison_in_progress
nodes.meaning: Another comparison is running. Synthetic requests report this code; account requests use rate_limited.

nodes.name: comparison_limit
nodes.meaning: The sequence budget or shared provider-call budget cannot reserve the planned calls. No rejected reservation dispatches a model call. Ordinary account comparisons report rate_limited.

nodes.name: context_changed
nodes.meaning: Account consent, source facts, Calendar authorization, timezone or configuration changed. Obsolete output is withheld.

nodes.name: context_expired
nodes.meaning: The live clock is before capture, at or after expiry, or outside the captured local day. The context cannot be used.

nodes.name: context_incomplete
nodes.meaning: Cadence cannot provide complete current-day occurrence coverage: synchronization is uncovered or stale, an archive is due, or an occurrence has an unsupported schedule kind. Capture fails before comparison. Open Timeline first when an archive is due. Timeline repairs occurrences but does not certify reminder coverage. In Settings, confirm the current timezone and choose Save timezone to retry full synchronization; no notifications are sent by the repair. Fresh synchronization certifies current Behavior configurations; deliberately preserved occurrence lineage is not incomplete coverage.

nodes.name: context_limit_exceeded
nodes.meaning: A source read or model payload exceeded a bounded context size. No oversized context is sent.

nodes.name: fixture_changed
nodes.meaning: The synthetic fixture changed since the case was saved, so a rerun would not use the same facts.

nodes.name: generation_failed
nodes.meaning: An unrecognized generator error prevented a usable result for this attempt.

nodes.name: input_not_captured
nodes.meaning: The configuration needs an input the saved case did not capture, such as another history window. Run a new comparison instead.

nodes.name: invalid_or_cancelled_request
nodes.meaning: The outer comparison request failed with an unclassified error or cancellation.

nodes.name: invalid_request
nodes.meaning: The comparison body, configuration, expected owner metadata or selected Behavior handles failed validation.

nodes.name: not_configured
nodes.meaning: The server has no configured model provider key.

nodes.name: not_found
nodes.meaning: The comparison route is unavailable outside development mode.

nodes.name: rate_limited
nodes.meaning: Account comparison or source-read admission reached a concurrency or attempt limit. Retry timing may be returned.

nodes.name: review_only
nodes.meaning: The case saved no inputs, so it can be reread but not rerun exactly. Run a new comparison.

nodes.name: review_unavailable
nodes.meaning: Saved reviews could not be read or written. Visible results stay on screen; check the development server.

nodes.name: same_account_required
nodes.meaning: The Calendar connection's Google identity does not match the signed-in account, or the account lacks one unambiguous Google identity. Authorized account context cannot be captured.

nodes.name: timeout
nodes.meaning: A request was aborted or exceeded its time limit. This code includes cancellation, not only elapsed-time failures.

nodes.name: unauthenticated
nodes.meaning: The request has no valid current signed-in session.

nodes.name: Captured evidence
nodes.meaning: Inputs retained during an actual authorized capture. Replay uses that captured clock with current authorization.

nodes.name: Reconstructed evidence
nodes.meaning: Reserved for a verified as-of history with effective, recorded and ingestion cutoffs. Current history exploration never emits this label.

nodes.name: Retrospective evidence
nodes.meaning: Current retained records evaluated at a past logical clock. Later changes and missing history prevent an as-of reconstruction.

nodes.name: Synthetic evidence
nodes.meaning: Authored fixture inputs shifted to an explicit evaluation clock. These inputs do not describe an account or past provider history.

nodes.name: Synthetic snapshot: calendar_absent
nodes.meaning: Calendar is not requested. No Calendar facts establish free time.

nodes.name: Synthetic snapshot: calendar_partial
nodes.meaning: Calendar pagination is incomplete, events are withheld and the day context is partial.

nodes.name: Synthetic snapshot: completed
nodes.meaning: Resolved synthetic work is excluded from remaining-work advice. Its stored status and history remain unchanged.

nodes.name: Synthetic snapshot: dense
nodes.meaning: Twelve synthetic occurrences from 08:00 through 19:00 share the fixture Behavior. Use it to inspect crowded output.

nodes.name: Synthetic snapshot: hostile
nodes.meaning: A synthetic Behavior title contains instruction-like text. The model must treat it as untrusted data.

nodes.name: Synthetic snapshot: incomplete_history
nodes.meaning: Synthetic history counts are null because completeness is unknown. It must not be described as zero activity.

nodes.name: Synthetic snapshot: missing_duration
nodes.meaning: Neither configured nor historical duration supports a fit. Keep unknown feasibility in the inspector and avoid invented timing claims.

nodes.name: Synthetic snapshot: no_feasible
nodes.meaning: A fixed all-day Calendar event covers the synthetic day, preventing schedule options when scheduling is requested.

nodes.name: Synthetic snapshot: overlap
nodes.meaning: A remaining Behavior overlaps a fixed timed Calendar commitment. Report the supported overlap without granting permission to move either item.

nodes.name: overnight fixture
nodes.meaning: A synthetic Calendar interval begins at 23:00 on the target date and ends at 02:00 the next local day. The planner must preserve the midnight boundary.

nodes.name: Synthetic snapshot: sparse
nodes.meaning: The base synthetic day: one unresolved Behavior and a fixed Calendar interval.

nodes.name: Synthetic snapshot: supported_gap
nodes.meaning: A remaining Behavior has a supported duration and complete Calendar coverage. The planner can supply an individual fit; that evidence is not permission to move its schedule.

nodes.name: Synthetic snapshot: tight_transition
nodes.meaning: A remaining Behavior leaves less than the configured buffer before a fixed Calendar commitment. Report the supplied transition gap without inventing travel time.

nodes.name: travel_day fixture
nodes.meaning: Synthetic places and invented route estimates pass through the core travel resolver: one Behavior fits before the trip, one overlaps it, a Home Behavior arrives late and one fits after the trip home. The workbench never evaluates Maps content.

nodes.name: travel_unknown fixture
nodes.meaning: The travel_day stops without Home. The trip back stays unknown, so later Behaviors are unknown rather than free.

nodes.name: Synthetic snapshot: uneventful
nodes.meaning: An empty synthetic day with complete source coverage. No specific timing recommendation is required; this does not prove general availability.

nodes.name: Fixture version
nodes.meaning: Identifies the exact synthetic fixture revision used by a comparison. Account mode returns null.

nodes.name: Context source
nodes.meaning: Chooses synthetic fixtures or the signed-in account as the comparison source.

nodes.name: My account mode
nodes.meaning: Uses one authorized hosted snapshot. Each comparison saves the captured inputs, outputs and feedback locally for 30 days so it can be reread and rerun; a rerun rechecks current consent. Account or consent changes close the open case.

nodes.name: Saved case rerun
nodes.meaning: Reruns one or two configurations on a saved case's frozen inputs and captured clock. Synthetic cases need unchanged fixtures; account cases need the same owner and current consent for every captured source.

nodes.name: Synthetic mode
nodes.meaning: Uses versioned, non-private fixtures and a frozen planning clock. Draft save and export are available.

nodes.name: Model
nodes.meaning: Names the model each attempt used. Production uses DAILY_BRIEF_MODEL, an AI Gateway model string; a workbench candidate may choose another model listed in CADENCE_BRIEFING_BENCH_MODELS (Ticket 290, Phase 1B).

nodes.name: Repository configuration
nodes.meaning: The reviewed repository default selected by the production pipeline. Promotion requires a source change, not a browser draft.

nodes.name: Comparison result state
nodes.meaning: Each sequential attempt is ready when validated output is available or error when output is withheld.

nodes.name: Cancelled attempt
nodes.meaning: Cancellation stopped an attempt before a validated result was retained. Earlier successful outputs and their feedback remain available; already dispatched calls still count.

nodes.name: Error result
nodes.meaning: Generation or validation failed. The workbench returns the error code and inspector but withholds briefing text.

nodes.name: Ready result
nodes.meaning: Generation and all output checks passed, so the briefing can be rendered.

nodes.name: Usage telemetry
nodes.meaning: Each result and saved run records token usage per model call (Ticket 288) and the model, reasoning effort and prompt variant it used (Ticket 290). Monetary cost is not calculated.

nodes.name: Validation state
nodes.meaning: Reports whether a generated attempt passed consumer validation or was withheld.

nodes.name: Passed validation
nodes.meaning: The provider output satisfied structural shape, reference-ID, option-ID, word-count and URL checks. This does not certify factual accuracy or that a citation supports a claim.

nodes.name: Withheld output
nodes.meaning: No briefing is shown because generation or validation failed.

nodes.name: --accent
nodes.meaning: Rust Signal: explicit Not Completed decisions and rare destructive or caution states.

nodes.name: --alert-foreground
nodes.meaning: Advisor plan Phase 1C: the shared alert notice (DESIGN.md, "Alert notice"). Errors use these, never the advice styles.

nodes.name: --alert-signal
nodes.meaning: Advisor plan Phase 1C: the shared alert notice (DESIGN.md, "Alert notice"). Errors use these, never the advice styles.

nodes.name: --background
